Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, our pediatrician recommended regular heart check-ups due to a familial history of cardiac issues. These check-ups help monitor her heart health closely and catch any potential problems early.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, she experiences hypotonia‚ which affects her muscle tone. This condition makes her muscles feel stiffer than they should be‚ and we're working with therapists to manage its impact on her daily life.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: She has constipation issues‚ which can be frustrating at times. Managing her diet and ensuring she stays hydrated helps alleviate these issues somewhat‚ but it's an ongoing challenge.

Parent: In addition to her specific health concerns‚ she takes longer to reach certain developmental milestones than her peers‚ and there are some palatal abnormalities we're monitoring closely with her healthcare team. These aspects require consistent attention and adaptation to ensure she receives the support she needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a familial history of cardiac issues and requires regular heart check-ups to monitor her heart health closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, which can be managed through diet and hydration adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects her muscle tone and requires therapeutic intervention to manage its impact on daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and necessitate regular hearing checks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has difficulty seeing distant objects clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods, requiring careful monitoring and possibly the need for corrective interventions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and frequent visits to the dentist are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has taken longer to reach certain developmental milestones than her peers and requires additional support and accommodations in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some individuals with KBG syndrome may need more support and some benefit from specialized settings, while others can thrive in mainstream environments with appropriate assistance.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and takes longer to achieve certain milestones compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit variability in their rate of development, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and there are palatal abnormalities that require close monitoring with her healthcare team.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various skeletal anomalies, including hip dysplasia, tethered cord, and anomalies of the palate, which can affect their overall physical development and mobility.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular heart check-ups are recommended due to a familial history of cardiac issues.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring her heart health closely, managing hypotonia, and considering therapeutic interventions based on specific symptoms and needs.
Note: N/A represents information that is not applicable to this patient.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences more frequent falls than other children his age, suggesting potential balance or coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have more significant neurological concerns such as tethered cord or skeletal anomalies.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid buildup in the ear, which may contribute to his hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasal grommet insertion to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects his vision and requires regular check-ups with an optometrist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as hypermetropia and squint (astigmatism).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent cavities, requiring regular dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues are common in KBG syndrome, including weak enamel and need for frequent dental procedures.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty reaching milestones such as walking and speaking, which impacts his educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some children needing support in mainstream settings and others possibly benefiting from specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences delays in various developmental areas, including speech, movement, and overall cognitive development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a common feature in KBG syndrome, with some children showing significant delay and others maintaining typical development.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with an increased incidence of skeletal anomalies, including hip dysplasia and tethered cord, which can affect mobility and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, eyesight (ophthalmology) review, and palatal review.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring heart valve abnormalities, treating tethered cord, managing palatal abnormalities, addressing feeding difficulties, and ensuring adequate nutrition.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect, which is a hole in the wall between the two upper chambers of the heart, requiring regular monitoring and medication to manage the condition effectively.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems occasionally, which can get quite uncomfortable for him. Dietary adjustments and advice from healthcare team have helped manage these issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and subtle anomalies of the palate can affect speech development and feeding, leading to considerations for specialist review in some cases.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting, and has been experiencing developmental delays. Specialists are keeping an eye on this to ensure it doesn't indicate any more serious underlying issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments. In a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media, an infection of the middle ear, which caused discomfort and affected his hearing temporarily but was successfully treated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means he has trouble seeing things that are far away, and corrective lenses have helped improve his vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision), and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent chipping or breaking of his teeth, requiring careful brushing and ensuring he doesn't bite into anything too hard.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental visits are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed extra help in school, with some children requiring support and others staying in mainstream education. However, overall educational attainment varies widely among individuals with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education levels range from those with mainstream qualifications to those with further education or independent careers. Some individuals may need support from family or friends with certain tasks, while others manage to live independently.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and is slower to achieve certain milestones, with specialists monitoring this to prevent future complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and palatal abnormalities that require periodic check-ups to ensure proper growth and alignment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can cause an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and palatal abnormalities that require monitoring to prevent further complications.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups are recommended to prevent further complications.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and medication are ongoing to manage heart conditions, address hormonal imbalances, and provide support for neurological, respiratory, and other health issues.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue and gets tired quickly, needing frequent breaks during physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movements that are too loose or hard, and has had to visit the bathroom multiple times during the night.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and constipation have been reported in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures and has difficulty keeping up with peers during physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to have fluid buildup in the ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear can cause conductive hearing loss in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to squint and get tired easily, suggesting potential visual strain.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty with harder foods and requires frequent dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental check-ups are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows delays in reaching developmental milestones and has difficulty keeping up with peers during physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome may experience challenges in mainstream education, requiring additional support or intervention.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and difficulty expressing herself clearly, leading to frustration.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may display behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which can impact their daily life.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study showed that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, eyesight (ophthalmology) review, and consideration for a palate review if feeding difficulties or speech concerns are present.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring for tethered cord, managing seizures, considering a cardiac review following diagnosis, evaluating palatal abnormalities, managing feeding difficulties, and ensuring adequate nutrition and overall health.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness easily when engaging in physical activities and requires a longer period to recover from exertion, suggesting possible cardiac involvement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, indicating variability in cardiac health among individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows feeding difficulties and selective eating habits, refusing to try new foods and being picky about meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are quite common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding and others experiencing constipation or other digestive issues.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic seizures, which require medication and lifestyle adjustments to manage the condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can vary in type and severity, and some may require surgery to remove seizure-causing tissue.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision clarity, particularly in situations with background noise.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, with some requiring corrective lenses and occasional surgeries.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit dentists frequently due to weak enamel and tooth sensitivity, necessitating gentle brushing techniques and regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues are not uncommon in KBG syndrome, including weak enamel, cavities, and gum problems, requiring periodic dental care and monitoring.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty expressing herself clearly and understanding complex concepts, impacting her academic performance and social interaction.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Students with KBG syndrome may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones and require additional support in school, including speech therapy and possibly behavioral interventions.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays developmental delays and has speech difficulties, making communication a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome typically experience delays in key areas such as mobility, self-help skills, and overall cognitive development, with some showing more pronounced delays than others.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and palatal abnormalities that may require intervention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with various skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones, hip dysplasia, and tethered cord, which can impact posture, movement, and overall alignment.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and vision assessments.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring for heart conditions, managing seizures, treating palatal abnormalities, and considering orthopedic interventions as needed.

Parent: Her front teeth are quite large compared to other kids her age. It's noticeable and sometimes affects her speech a little bit. I'm planning to take her to see an orthodontist soon.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Parent: N/A.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires regular cardiac check-ups to monitor the situation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be quite picky with food and often refuses to eat certain things, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring off into space and seeming unresponsive for a few seconds, which are unsettling but currently non-consequential.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had glue ear, which has been treated and her hearing is now normal.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, requiring glasses to correct her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision), and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty eating certain foods and requires gentle yet thorough toothbrushing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and developmental differences, which impact her ability to express herself clearly and engage fully in lessons.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some children with KBG syndrome require additional support, while others excel in mainstream settings. Levels of educational attainment vary widely, with some obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring and unresponsiveness, which can be concerning but are currently benign.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit various delays, including speech delay, palatal abnormalities, and movement disorders. Monitoring and support are crucial to identify and address these challenges.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with an increased incidence of skeletal anomalies, including hip dysplasia, tethered cord, and asymmetric hip creases, which can affect mobility and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, regular hearing reviews, periodic eye check-ups to age 5, and consideration of a palate review if feeding difficulties or speech concerns are present.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Addressing septal defects, monitoring hormonal imbalances, managing neurological conditions, correcting palatal abnormalities, and considering orthopedic interventions as needed.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in her heart that requires regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is slower to gain weight compared to other kids her age and has difficulty eating enough.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes where she stares off into space and doesn't respond for a few seconds, which is worrying and is being managed with physical therapy and exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid in the ear, which has led to conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision) and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel and requires regular dental check-ups to prevent any more problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty gaining weight and has speech delay, which is being worked on with a speech therapist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though some may require more support and some benefit from a specialist setting.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring and lack of responsiveness, which are concerning and are being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups.

Parent: Oh, yes! My child often complains that things look blurry to him. I've noticed he squints a lot when watching TV or playing video games, and he says it's hard to see clearly. I'm really worried about his eyesight, to be honest.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Well, sometimes I call his name and he doesn't respond right away. It's like he's not hearing me or is too engrossed in what he's doing to notice. I've had to repeat myself a few times before he reacts.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: He's been complaining about tooth sensitivity lately, especially when he eats cold foods like ice cream or drinks cold water. It's gotten to the point where he avoids certain foods because of the discomfort.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... the doctors found a valve issue in his heart. I'm constantly worried about it, to be frank. We go for regular check-ups and try to keep an eye on how it might be affecting him.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He's had seizures. They started a while back and have been a source of great concern for us. We're working closely with the neurologist to manage them.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Bowel movements have been a bit of an issu. He's experienced some irregularities and discomfort that we're trying to address through diet and lifestyle changes.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: My child isn't speaking as much as I'd expect for his age. It's worrying since he should be communicating more by now. I just want to make sure everything possible is done to help him catch up.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in his heart, which requires regular check-ups and monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel irregularities and discomfort, which are being managed through diet and lifestyle changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and constipation have been reported in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are being managed through medication and close monitoring by a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can vary in type and severity.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hearing difficulties, including blurred vision and discomfort with certain foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences vision problems such as astigmatism and squint, which are being monitored and treated as needed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia, hypermetropia, and astigmatism.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and discomfort with cold foods, requiring careful brushing and avoiding certain foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and frequent cavities are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty expressing himself effectively, leading to frustration and a desire to communicate more.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some benefiting from specialized settings and others remaining in mainstream education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows delays in reaching developmental milestones and has speech delay, which is being addressed through various therapies.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a common feature in KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as "typical" children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine, and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience hip dysplasia, which can affect movement and positioning, and palatal abnormalities that may impact feeding and speech development.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and periodic review of heart health.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and managing seizure activity, addressing hormonal imbalances, correcting palatal abnormalities, treating tethered cord, managing feeding difficulties, and ensuring proper nutrition and dental care.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation and has bowel movement concerns, managed through balancing her diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a speech delay, and her balance seems off sometimes, leading to frequent falls.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid buildup in the ear, which has impacted her hearing and balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of her eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, can occasionally be a feature in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups to maintain oral health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental procedures may be more common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, with some children needing more support and others benefiting from specialized settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring additional support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits speech delay, difficulty with balance, and falls more often than peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have various behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A small number of children with KBG syndrome have had hip dysplasia, where the hip joints are easily dislocated.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, eyesight (ophthalmology) review, and consideration for palatal review if feeding difficulties or speech concerns are present.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve issue, treatment of tethered cord, management of palatal abnormalities, management of hip dysplasia, and consideration of speech therapy and physical therapy based on individual needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular monitoring by a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a slower rate of weight gain compared to her peers, which is being discussed with her pediatrician to rule out any underlying issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epilepsy, which is managed through regular sessions with a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which has led to conductive hearing loss and required grommet insertion and hearing aid use.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had issues with fluid buildup in the ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and palatal abnormalities, which are being addressed through speech therapy and palate review.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, which are being monitored and treated as necessary.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty with hard foods and prefers softer options, suggesting potential dental concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and is receiving therapy to address this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some individuals with KBG syndrome have required additional support and some have gone on to further education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and palatal abnormalities, which are affecting her development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may experience delays in reaching milestones such as walking, sitting, and using cutlery and zips.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which may lead to an increased curvature of the spine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletally, some individuals with KBG syndrome have shorter fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and periodic checks for palatal abnormalities.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring heart condition, managing epilepsy, addressing gastrointestinal concerns, providing speech therapy, correcting postural issues, and considering orthopedic interventions as needed.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: Yes... two things. First， his fingers are noticeably shorter than his friends'. And secondly... he has scoliosis. The specialist said it's something we'll need to monitor closely as he grows.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son often squints when trying to focus on things, which makes us worry about his eyesight. It's not just when reading or watching TV; it happens even when he's playing or looking at pictures.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: We've noticed he seems to pick up on some sounds but completely misses others, even when they're pretty loud. It's like he's filtering out certain frequencies or something. We're not sure what's going on, but it's definitely affected his ability to follow conversations sometimes.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth are very prone to breaking or chipping. We have to be super careful with what he eats and make sure he brushes them gently but thoroughly. It's been a challenge since he was little, and we're always on the lookout for any signs of tooth decay or damage.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, there's a structural issue with his heart that the cardiologist keeps an eye on. We go for regular check-ups to monitor it closely. So far, it hasn't held him back from playing or running around with his friends, but we do have to keep it in mind when considering physical activities.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He experiences seizures. They can be scary, but we've learned how to manage them better over time. His neurologist is great and helps us adjust his medication as needed.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: When he was a baby, feeding was a real challenge. He had trouble latching on and would get frustrated easily. Thankfully, that phase passed, and now he eats fairly normally.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the heart condition and seizures, our main concern now is his scoliosis. It affects his posture and can cause back pain if not managed properly. Additionally, he struggles to express himself clearly; it's hard for him to find the right words or explain what he wants or needs. We're working on that with speech therapy.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that requires regular monitoring by a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties as a baby, including trouble latching on and getting frustrated easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures and has neurological issues that require management through medication adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have complications related to their neurological development.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that affect his breathing and feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some experience speech delays or clarity issues.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects his vision and ability to focus on distant objects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frequent tooth breakages and chipping, requiring gentle yet thorough brushing to prevent further damage.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth are prone to breaking or chipping in individuals with KBG syndrome, and regular dental care is crucial to prevent additional issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges in school that require support through EHCP plans and occasional need for extended periods of rest.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education levels vary among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some achieving mainstream qualifications and others needing more support in mainstream settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including speech clarity issues and difficulty expressing himself effectively.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety are commonly observed in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which impacts his posture and causes discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can lead to various complications such as pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and periodic review for palatal abnormalities.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring heart condition, managing seizures, treating palatal abnormalities, managing scoliosis, and providing speech therapy as needed.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has hypermetropia, which means he has a hard time seeing things up close. It's been a challenge for him during activities that require attention to detail.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, he often asks people to repeat themselves because he doesn't catch everything the first time around. This can get frustrating at times, especially in noisy environments where it's already tough to focus.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing harder foods is a bit of an ordeal for him. The dentist says his teeth are otherwise healthy, but we need to be mindful of what he eats to avoid discomfort or pain.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Physical activities that last a long time are really challenging for our boy. He gets tired easily and can't keep up with his peers when they're playing sports or running around. We're working on finding exercises that suit him better.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He experiences hypotonia‚ which affects his muscle tone. It's something we're managing with therapy and exercise to help improve his overall strength and coordination.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been a significant issue due to a strong aversion he has. Mealtime can be stressful‚ but we're learning ways to make it more enjoyable and less confrontational for everyone involved.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Two additional concerns we have are the delayed fontanelle closure‚ which the doctors are monitoring closely‚ and his struggles with clarity when trying to communicate. Sometimes‚ it takes him a few attempts to express himself clearly‚ but with patience and support‚ he's making progress.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue during physical activities and challenges with keeping up with peers during sports or running around, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, indicating variability in cardiac health among individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties due to a strong aversion, making mealtime stressful and requiring strategies to make it more enjoyable and less confrontational.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and is managed with therapy and exercise to improve his strength and coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, and some may require surgery.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had otitis media or glue ear, and regular hearing checks are recommended to prevent further complications.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects his ability to see things up close, leading to frustration during close-up activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, which may impact their daily life.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires careful consideration of what he eats to avoid discomfort or pain, and regular dental check-ups are essential.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are necessary to prevent infections and ensure proper oral hygiene.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, with some children needing support in mainstream settings and others benefiting from specialized settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring more support. The transition to further education and adult life also differs greatly depending on individual circumstances.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including hypotonia and speech clarity challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which can impact their daily lives and interactions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and there are concerns regarding tethered cord and hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait. Monitoring and treatment are crucial to address these conditions effectively.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups, periodic hearing reviews, and monitoring of fontanelle closure and palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may need ongoing monitoring for heart conditions, tethered cord, and other associated anomalies, ensuring timely intervention and management to minimize complications and promote optimal health and wellbeing.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing when playing, faster than what is considered normal.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's heart rate increases rapidly when engaging in physical activity, which is monitored by the pediatrician.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows a strong aversion to eating certain foods, particularly vegetables and meat.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and palatal abnormalities can be observed in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires more quickly than other kids when running around or playing, suggesting potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have cognitive delays and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced fluid buildup in the ear, which is managed by doctors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear can lead to conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, where his eyes focus on objects far away rather than nearby.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent cavities, requiring regular dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care should be closely monitored, especially for those with weak enamel and high cavity rates.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to reach developmental milestones and requires additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some children with KBG syndrome may need more support, while others excel in mainstream settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and takes longer to achieve certain milestones compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, there is a wide range of abilities among people with KBG syndrome, from those with no delay to those with significant challenges.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletally, some individuals with KBG syndrome may experience hip dysplasia, where the hip joints are easily dislocated.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiology assessments.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve changes, treatment of fluid buildup in the ear, management of palatal abnormalities, and consideration of speech therapy and physiotherapy based on individual needs.
